title: Cheezechoice
description: A food delivery service website designed to make local ordering feel fast and friendly.
imageCaption: A warm, clear interface keeps the menu and ordering flow easy to scan.
body: Cheezechoice is a food delivery service website built around quick discovery and a simple path to checkout.

title: Code 365
description: A full-stack learning and interview-prep platform with 360+ DSA problems, SQL practice, interactive visualizers, and company-specific preparation.
imageCaption: A structured learning experience helps developers build skills and prepare for technical interviews.
body: Code 365 is a full-stack platform for developers learning data structures and algorithms, practicing SQL, and preparing for technical interviews. It brings together more than 360 coding problems, a SQL problem bank, daily challenges, flashcards, and structured study plans.

I approached the product as a complete learning loop: give people a clear next step, let them practice hands-on, and help them see their progress. The Monaco-based editor supports coding practice, while algorithm, Git, and SQL tools make concepts easier to explore through interaction.

Interview resources—including mock interviews, company-wise questions, and interview experiences—connect that practice to real hiring goals. Streaks, statistics, achievements, and rankings add ways to track momentum over time.

I built the platform with Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Radix UI. Supabase provides authentication and the PostgreSQL database, with Gemini integration supporting AI features. The application is deployed on Vercel.

title: Smart Mart
description: A full-stack shopping experience with product discovery, cart and wishlist, order management, secure authentication, and payment integration.
imageCaption: A clear checkout flow connects the product catalog, cart, and order process.
body: Smart Mart is a full-stack ecommerce platform built to make the path from browsing to checkout straightforward. Shoppers can explore a product catalog, manage a cart and wishlist, place orders, and access generated invoices.

The project brings together the customer-facing storefront and the services behind it. The Angular and Angular Material frontend connects to a Spring Boot and Hibernate backend, with support for secure authentication and persistent product and order data.

content.text: Smart Mart is designed around the everyday shopping journey: find a product, decide whether to save it or add it to the cart, and move through a clear order flow. The catalog, cart, wishlist, order history, and invoice generation support that journey from discovery through purchase.

content.alt: Produce arranged in a grocery store
content.caption: Product discovery is the first step in the shopping flow.

content.text: I built the application as a full-stack system. Angular and Angular Material provide the responsive storefront, while Spring Boot and Hibernate handle backend services. The project supports MySQL or PostgreSQL and includes JWT-based authentication to protect customer and order workflows.

content.alt: A customer using a payment card at checkout
content.caption: The checkout flow brings cart and payment into one clear path.

content.text: The purchase experience includes payment gateway integration, order processing, and invoice generation. A customer support chatbot adds another way to get help, while Google Analytics provides insight into traffic and customer behavior.

On the operational side, Log4j supports application logging and audit trails. Together, these pieces make Smart Mart more than a static storefront: it connects shopping, payment, support, and monitoring in one application.

title: Drona LMS
description: A production-ready, microservice-ready LMS foundation with a Spring Boot backend, PostgreSQL, JWT authentication, and a separately planned AI service.
imageCaption: A modular service foundation for learning management and future AI capabilities.
body: Drona LMS is a production-ready, microservice-ready foundation for a learning management system. The current backend uses Java 17 and Spring Boot, with PostgreSQL persistence and JWT-based authentication secured by Spring Security.

I organized the workspace around separate services: the Spring Boot backend, an Angular frontend, and a FastAPI AI service. The frontend and AI service are planned components, with architecture, database, and endpoint documentation guiding their integration.
The stack is designed to run together with Docker Compose. The project currently uses NeonDB for hosted database storage, with a migration to AWS planned.
